features.contract: The built binary serves the document, CSS, JavaScript, and favicon without external runtime requests or JavaScript errors.
Loading, empty, failed graph, visible retry, and recovery states remain operable.
The header and empty state expose copyable MCP, OTLP gRPC, and OTLP HTTP endpoints.
The pulse and map show deterministic gateway to checkout telemetry, including the process uptime readout.
The map retains zoom, fit, and minimap overview navigation.
Search filters services, selection opens the inspector, and selection survives in URL state.
Overview metrics and dependency direction remain available in the inspector.
Why and Impact call the real MCP tools, and Impact can hand the downstream cone back to the map.
The command palette retains navigation, service selection, triage actions, theme toggle, and MCP URL copy commands.
Named controls, search focus, inspector tabs, service activation, and the shortcut sheet remain keyboard operable.
The UI reports a dropped server, reconnects to the same binary and database, and retains the topology after refetch.
Light and dark themes use the project token system and persist across reload.
At 390 by 844, map and list navigation plus the inspector remain operable without page overflow.

Host mode draws every host from /api/hosts as a diamond node in the service layout with one dashed runs-on edge per service placement, excluded from call traversals so the blast radius is unchanged; the list groups by host, host entities stay out of the service ranking, and the host panel reads CPU, memory and disk through /api/metrics or says not reported; toggle, host nodes and host chips are keyboard reachable and the grouped list stays readable on mobile.
The tracked client has no Node manifest, lockfile, frontend build, generated bundle, remote font, CDN import, or external design-system package.
The README remains user focused and covers install, first telemetry, UI, MCP, common configuration, and production links.
